newsitem.title: INDIA: Stanchart cuts Indian lending rate to 18.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Stanchart cuts Indian lending rate to 18.0 pct.

text.p: Standard Chartered Bank said on Saturday it has cut its Indian prime lending rate by 0.5 percentage points to 18.0 percent from 18.5 percent effective September 30.
The cut was "to keep in line with current trend in prime lending rates", a bank official said.
The reduction was the second in less than three months. On July 15, the bank cut the rate by 1.0 percentage point to 18.5 percent from 19.5 percent, the official said.

Several domestic banks led by the State Bank of India, the country's largest commercial bank, cut their prime lending rate to 15.5 percent earlier this month due to slowing industrial demand for funds.
The prime rate is the interest banks charge their blue-chip clients. Loans to other companies carry higher interest rates.
